review.notes: Text lineage is cosmetic throughout: v0 (AST-047, 2004-06-01) 'until the end of the End Phase' -> v1 (SD10-EN034, 2007-01-17) 'until the end of this turn' is the same duration and both scripts reset the DEF change at RESET_PHASE+PHASE_END; v1 -> v2 (SD10-EN034 reprinted in Machine Madness Value Box, 2014-02-28) is PSCT targeting wording only, and both scripts already carry EFFECT_FLAG_CARD_TARGET, so targeting did not change. Verified aux.StatChangeDamageStepCondition (cardscripts/utility.lua:1412) and RESETS_STANDARD_PHASE_END (cardscripts/constant.lua:300) directly, which is what reduces the diff to the single property flag. Not redundant with the engine rule profile: docs/research/ocgcore-flags.md establishes that DUEL_MODE_GOAT's damage-step flags (DUEL_6_STEP_BATLLE_STEP, DUEL_SINGLE_CHAIN_IN_DAMAGE_SUBSTEP) govern chain windows only and that no DUEL_ flag exists for per-card pre-errata behaviour, while per-effect damage-step activation legality lives in the script's EFFECT_FLAG_DAMAGE_STEP/EFFECT_FLAG_DAMAGE_CAL property. Because the chronology is unresolved the applier will block format selection rather than pick a version; that is preferred here to inventing a date.

event.historical_text: The DEF of 1 face-up monster on the field becomes 0 until the end of the End Phase.
event.summary: Period damage-step legality, not a text erratum: the GOAT variant declares the activation with EFFECT_FLAG_DAMAGE_CAL where the modern script declares EFFECT_FLAG_DAMAGE_STEP, so the era card is activatable during damage calculation itself rather than only in the pre-damage-calculation part of the Damage Step. Its inline condition (Duel.GetCurrentPhase()~=PHASE_DAMAGE or not Duel.IsDamageCalculated()) is logically identical to the modern aux.StatChangeDamageStepCondition (utility.lua: not (Duel.IsPhase(PHASE_DAMAGE) and Duel.IsDamageCalculated())), and the SetReset line is only RESETS_STANDARD_PHASE_END written out, so the property flag is the sole behavioural difference. No source in the packet dates the damage-step rule change, so the chronology is left unresolved.
